cards.text: Friend, things are tense. While Moses, Israel's leader, was up on the mountain, the people made a golden calf and bowed down to it (Exodus 32:8). Now the LORD tells Moses to leave this place with the people and go to the land He promised to Israel's forefathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

cards.question: God says He will drive out the Canaanites, the Amorites and the other nations in the land. He'll also send someone ahead of the people. Who?

cards.text: It's a land flowing with milk and honey. Sounds perfect, right? Then God says the next part, and it is NOT the part anybody wanted.

cards.question: God says He Himself will go with the people to the land.
God won't go with the people because they are a stiff-necked people. He says if He did go with them, He might ___ them on the way.

cards.text: The people hear this bad news, and they go into mourning. A whole camp making the face you make when your boss says, "Hey, got a minute?"

cards.question: As the people mourn, no one puts on any of his ___.

cards.text: The LORD had already given Moses a message for them. You are stiff-necked, and if I went with you for a single moment, I would destroy you.

cards.question: In that message, the LORD tells the Israelites to take off their jewelry, and He will decide what to do with them.

cards.text: So from Mount Horeb onward, the Israelites strip off their jewelry. Me? The only jewelry I've ever owned is the flour stuck in my mustache.
Now the story shows us something Moses used to do. He'd take a tent and pitch it, and he called it the Tent of Meeting.

cards.question: Where does Moses pitch the Tent of Meeting?

answers.text: At a distance outside the camp
Right in the middle of the camp
Up on top of the mountain

cards.question: The Tent of Meeting wasn't just for Moses. Anyone inquiring of the LORD would go out to it.
Whenever Moses walks out to the Tent of Meeting, what does the rest of the camp do?

answers.text: Stand at their tent doors and watch him
Follow him all the way out there
Stay inside with the flaps closed

cards.text: Every eye in the camp follows him until he's inside. Then, as Moses enters, something comes down and stays right at the entrance.

cards.question: As Moses enters the Tent of Meeting, the pillar of ___ comes down and stays at the entrance.
When the people see the pillar of cloud at the tent, they stand up and worship, each one at the entrance to his own tent.
Inside the Tent of Meeting, the LORD speaks with Moses. How?

answers.text: Face to face like a friend

cards.text: Then Moses heads back to camp. But one person is NOT leaving that tent, and honestly, that's me at the oven door when the batch has two minutes left.

cards.question: When Moses goes back to the camp, who stays in the Tent of Meeting?

cards.text: Now Moses talks to the LORD. He says, You keep telling me to lead this people up, but You haven't let me know whom You will send with me.

cards.question: Moses reminds the LORD that He said He knows Moses by name.

cards.text: So Moses makes a request. If he really has found favor in God's sight, there's something he wants.

cards.question: Moses asks the LORD to let him know His ways, so that Moses may know Him and find favor in His sight.
Moses adds, "Remember that this nation is Your people." What does the LORD answer?

answers.text: His Presence will go and give rest
His prophets will go and guide them
Moses will go and lead them alone

cards.text: Moses replies, If Your Presence doesn't go with us, don't lead us up from here. Translation: this car is NOT leaving the driveway without You.

cards.question: Moses says God going with them is how it can be known that something is true. What?

answers.text: They have found favor in His sight
They are the strongest nation on earth
Moses is the greatest leader of all

cards.question: Moses also says God going with them is how they will be set apart from all the other people on the face of the earth.

cards.text: The LORD says He will do this very thing Moses asked. If God told me yes, I'd back out of the room slowly before anybody changed their mind, but Moses asks for something even BIGGER.

cards.question: Moses asks the LORD to show him His ___.

cards.text: The LORD says He will cause all His goodness to pass before Moses. ALL of it, friend.

cards.question: The LORD also says He will proclaim something in Moses's presence. What?

cards.text: Then He says, “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion.” But He adds one limit.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses he can see His face.
Why can't Moses see the LORD's face?

answers.text: No one can see Him and live

cards.text: The LORD has it all arranged: there's a place near Him where Moses is to stand upon a rock. Meanwhile, I can't remember where I set down my rolling pin five minutes ago.

cards.question: No one can see the LORD's face and live. So when His glory passes by, what will He do for Moses standing on that rock?

answers.text: Put him in the rock and cover him with His hand
Send him back inside the Tent of Meeting
Tell him to close his eyes and kneel down

cards.text: His hand stays over Moses until He has passed by. Then He will take His hand away.

cards.question: When the LORD takes His hand away, Moses will see His ___.

cards.text: His back, but His face must not be seen. Hang on to that picture of Moses tucked in the rock, friend, because this story keeps going and I'm not about to spoil it.

findings.problem: Too many choices require prior knowledge or luck rather than reasoning from the earlier cards. Cards 2, 5, 12, 13, 14, 16 and 20 ask for unrevealed details: who is sent, what God might do, where the tent is pitched, who may use it, what the camp does, what comes down and who stays. For example, card 15 says only that "something" comes down before card 16 asks for "cloud," and card 19 gives no clue about who stays before card 20. Seven of the twelve choices being discovery questions is more than the allowed few.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "It's a land flowing with milk and honey," "Sounds perfect, right?" and "Then God says the next part...." Only the opening card may have three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: "False" is correct for verse 3, but the statement is not limited to that moment. God later says, "My Presence will go with you" (Exodus 33:14), and grants Moses's request that He go with "us" (Exodus 33:15-17). Consequently, the wrong option "True" is not false everywhere in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: "In that message" points back to the message introduced on story card 8, which is no longer on screen. The question should identify the LORD's message to the Israelites without relying on that earlier card.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: This story card is punctuated as three sentences: the Israelites stripping off their jewelry, "Me?" and the sentence about flour in Papa Dorin's mustache. It exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card says that the LORD will do what Moses asked but omits His stated reason in verse 17: Moses has found favor in His sight, and He knows Moses by name. God's own confirmation of those things explains His answer and completes Moses's appeal from verses 12-13, so this is an important detail to leave out.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "That rock" points back to the rock introduced on story card 16. The question should supply its own context, such as identifying it as the rock near the LORD where Moses is standing.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The picture of Moses "tucked in the rock" uses verse 22, where the LORD puts him in a cleft of the rock and covers him, but the card cites only verse 23. Its citation should run from Exodus 33:22 through Exodus 33:23.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
